subject: Proposal: renewal overlay — incremental commit swing + temporary rate moratorium
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@openretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@openretail.com
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing: options for next term

Hi Marissa,

We’re starting renewal planning for OpenRetail — our usage has been ramping faster than forecast and we expect a meaningful uplift next term (roughly 2x current committed throughput). Before we get legal involved we’d like to understand what flexibility Redwood can offer around:

- Short-term capacity swings during onboarding of new product features
- Temporary price protections for the first 60–90 days as we onboard additional users
- Any credits or true‑up mechanics for sudden spikes

Can you send a couple of concrete options (pricing + operational guardrails) that we can review with procurement? Timeline: we want a draft by the end of next week if possible.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Chen
CFO, OpenRetail Inc

--
OpenRetail procurement: procurement@openretail.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@openretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing: options for next term

Laura — thanks for the context. Attached is a short draft (redwood-renewal-draft-terms-v2.pdf) and our usage export for Q2 so you can see the math we used (usage-report-q2.csv).

High-level options (so you can weigh tradeoffs quickly):

Option A — Growth Commitment + Small Discount
- 2x annual commit (12-month term)
- 10% off published commitment price for new commit tier
- Standard true‑up at quarter close
- No moratorium on rate changes

Option B — Incremental Commit Swing + 90‑day Rate Moratorium (recommended)
- Increase commit to 1.6x (gives runway vs immediate 2x)
- Temporary moratorium: for the first 90 days, any additional consumption above previous run‑rate billed at prior term price (i.e., price held for short onboarding window)
- On top of that, a one‑time 25% credit applied to overage tokens that exceed 150% of prior quarter baseline during the moratorium window
- 6% discount on new commit price vs published list

Option C — Paygo + Bridge Credits
- Keep current commit, give expanded burst pool at a blended rate and issue credits for sustained usage above burst threshold

My read: Option B balances your desire for predictability during ramp (moratorium + credits) while keeping us aligned on a multi‑month commit. If you want, I can lock the terms and route to legal for an amendment once we agree.

Proposed next step: 30 minute call Friday 10–10:30am PT to walk through the numbers. Are you available?

—

1) Financial impact: are we comfortable with 6% discount on the new commit + one‑time 25% overage credit applied only for moratorium window? Can we map expected revenue vs downside if they exceed 2x earlier than forecast?
2) Operational: what SLOs / burst pool rules should we include so ops can enforce predictable behavior (e.g., burst cap, notification thresholds, auto‑fallback to paygo)?

I’ve attached a short note and the usage export. Call Friday at 10PT to prep?

Marissa

Marissa — I ran a sensitivity on Option B and attached a spreadsheet (pricing-sensitivity-openretail.xlsx). Quick take:

- 6% discount at 1.6x commit: expected net ARR change is +22% vs current year if they trend to 1.6x over 12 months.
- 90‑day moratorium with a one‑time 25% overage credit is reasonable if we bound the moratorium: apply only to the delta above prior run‑rate up to an absolute ceiling (suggest ceiling = 2.5x prior run‑rate)
- Add a hard burst cap during moratorium (e.g., 3x hourly burst but billed as overage beyond 2.5x and then throttled after 4x sustained for 10 minutes) — that gives us predictable worst‑case and protects capacity for other customers.
- Finance asks we keep an audit window: any moratorium credits are reconciled at quarter close and applied as a credit memo, not as discounted unit price permanently.

If you want to be slightly more conservative, reduce discount to 5% and make moratorium credits tiered (25% up to 175% baseline, 15% 175–250%). Happy to present these variants on the call Friday.

Ben
Head of Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 04 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Final draft: Incremental commit + temporary rate moratorium (proposal)

Laura — thanks for the call last week. Per our discussion, attached is the proposal we’ll route to legal if you sign off: redwood-renewal-draft-terms-v2.pdf (final), plus the pricing sensitivity Ben ran.

Summary of what we’ll include in the amendment:
- Term: 12 months starting on execution date
- Commit: 1.6x current annualized run‑rate (commit ladder in doc)
- Discount: 6% off published commit price for new commit tier
- Moratorium: 90 calendar days from effective date — during this window, additional consumption above prior run‑rate will be billed at prior term price and a one‑time credit applied to the delta (25% credit up to 2.5x prior run‑rate; tiered after that per Ben’s spreadsheet)
- Operational guardrails: 3x hourly burst cap during moratorium, automatic notifications at 125% and 150% thresholds, and auto‑fallback to paygo above 4x sustained for 10 minutes
- Reconciliation: credits issued as a credit memo at quarter close; usage audited by both parties

Next step: please confirm (Reply All) that you’re happy to proceed and I’ll ask legal to produce an amendment (DocuSign link will follow). If you prefer a slightly smaller discount (5%) we can toggle that prior to legal — Ben recommended the current numbers as the best balance.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing our partnership.

—
